title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Longitudinal Care Pathway

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with type 2 diabetes in primary care: diagnosis, individualised HbA1c targets, lifestyle, metformin and add-on therapy by comorbidity (ASCVD, heart failure, CKD), insulin initiation and titration, cardiovascular risk management and complication screening. Verified against the Saudi Diabetes Clinical Practice Guidelines (SDCPG, Saudi National Diabetes Center/Saudi Health Council, 2021); doses and contraindications from US FDA prescribing information. DKA, HHS and hypoglycaemia are covered in their own topics.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: SDCPG statin figures (12–13) not reproduced as text
NICE NG28 not re-reviewed for this version
Ramadan-specific dose adjustments — SDCPG Ramadan section/local protocol

pathophysiology.summary: Type 2 diabetes results from insulin resistance (liver, muscle, adipose tissue) combined with progressive beta-cell failure, producing chronic hyperglycaemia. It is strongly linked to obesity, inactivity and family history; Saudi Arabia has one of the highest prevalences worldwide.
keyMechanisms: Insulin resistance (visceral fat, ectopic fat in liver and muscle) raises insulin demand; beta-cell dysfunction and loss mean insulin secretion cannot keep up → fasting and post-meal hyperglycaemia.
Increased hepatic glucose output (target of metformin), reduced incretin effect (GLP-1 RA, DPP-4 inhibitors) and increased renal glucose reabsorption (SGLT2 inhibitors).
Progressive disease: most people need treatment intensification over time, eventually insulin.
Chronic hyperglycaemia causes microvascular (retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy) and macrovascular (coronary, cerebrovascular, peripheral arterial) disease.
HbA1c below 7% reduces microvascular complications; SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs with proven benefit reduce cardiovascular, heart failure and kidney outcomes.

symptoms: Polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision.
Recurrent infections: genital candidiasis, UTIs, skin infections; slow wound healing.
physicalSigns: Reduced foot sensation (10-g monofilament, 128-Hz tuning fork), foot ulcers.
redFlags: Glucose above 300 mg/dL or HbA1c above 10% with weight loss or osmotic symptoms — start insulin (SDCPG)
Foot ulcer, infection or ischaemia — urgent foot team
precipitants: Previous gestational diabetes or macrosomic baby
Drugs: glucocorticoids, atypical antipsychotics, statins, thiazides

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Younger, lean, ketosis, positive islet antibodies, low C-peptide.
Strong family history, young onset, non-obese.
Pancreatic disease, steroids, Cushing's, acromegaly, drugs (antipsychotics, statins).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Diabetes: fasting 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or more; 2-h OGTT 200 mg/dL (11.1) or more; HbA1c 6.5% or more; random 200 mg/dL or more with symptoms. Prediabetes: fasting 100–125 mg/dL, 2-h 140–199, HbA1c 5.7–6.4%.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Confirm an asymptomatic abnormal result with a repeat test.

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose and assess
actions: Confirm diagnosis (fasting glucose, OGTT, HbA1c or random glucose with symptoms).
Assess ASCVD, heart failure and CKD at least annually — these choose second-line drugs (SDCPG).
Baseline eye, foot, kidney, lipid and BP assessment; screen for depression annually.

clinicalManagement.title: Set targets
actions: HbA1c below 7% for most adults; 6.5% if achievable safely; up to 8% for frail, hypoglycaemia-prone or limited life expectancy (SDCPG).
BP below 130/80 if achievable (SDCPG Figure 11); statin per risk; smoking cessation.

clinicalManagement.title: First-line
actions: Structured education, medical nutrition therapy and physical activity; weight loss 7% or more if overweight.
Metformin first unless contraindicated (safe if eGFR above 30).
HbA1c more than 1.5% above target at diagnosis: start dual therapy.
HbA1c above 10%, glucose above 300 mg/dL or catabolic symptoms: start insulin (or GLP-1 RA) (SDCPG).

clinicalManagement.title: Add-on therapy
clinicalManagement.timeframe: If not at target after about 3 months
actions: ASCVD: SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA with proven CV benefit.
Heart failure (or high risk of HF): SGLT2 inhibitor.
CKD: SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA shown to slow CKD progression.
No ASCVD/CKD: any of sulfonylurea, pioglitazone, DPP-4 inhibitor, SGLT2 inhibitor, GLP-1 RA or basal insulin, chosen by hypoglycaemia risk, weight, cost and preference.
Need a bigger glucose-lowering effect from an injectable: GLP-1 RA. Re-evaluate every 3–6 months; do not delay intensification.

clinicalManagement.title: Insulin
actions: Basal insulin 0.1–0.2 units/kg/day if HbA1c below 8%, or 0.2–0.3 units/kg/day if above 8%; titrate by 2 units every 3 days to fasting target (SDCPG).
Add prandial insulin with the largest meal: 4–5 units or 10% of basal dose; titrate by 1–2 units (or 10%) every 2–3 days to 2-h post-meal target.
Premixed insulin 2–3 times daily is an option. Review every 2 weeks on initiation; check injection technique and sites.

clinicalManagement.title: Cardiovascular and kidney protection
actions: Statin per SDCPG Figures 12–13; ACE inhibitor or ARB for hypertension with albuminuria; aspirin for secondary prevention.
Hold metformin on the day of iodinated contrast and restart after 1–2 days once renal function is confirmed stable (SDCPG).

learningObjectives: Diagnose type 2 diabetes and manage glycaemia, cardiovascular and kidney risk, and complications over time.

keyPoints: Metformin first; dual therapy if HbA1c 1.5% above target.
ASCVD/HF/CKD: SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA regardless of HbA1c.
Basal insulin 0.1–0.3 units/kg, titrate 2 units every 3 days.
Annual eyes, feet, ACR/eGFR and lipids.
pitfalls: Sulfonylureas in frail or fasting patients.
No sick-day rules for SGLT2 inhibitors/metformin.

patientEducation: Hypoglycaemia recognition and treatment; sick-day rules.
Foot care and annual eye checks; Ramadan planning.
lifestyleAndDiet: Healthy eating pattern (e.g. Mediterranean/DASH), reduce sugary drinks.
150 minutes/week moderate activity plus resistance exercise.
Weight loss of 7% or more if overweight; stop smoking.
mdtReferrals: Ophthalmology at diagnosis and by retinopathy status.
Endocrinology for complex insulin regimens or atypical diabetes.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review every 3 months until at target, then every 3–6 months: HbA1c, weight, BP, hypoglycaemia, adherence; annually: ACR/eGFR, lipids, eye and foot examination, depression screen, CVD/HF/CKD reassessment.
